article.title: K Foundation Burn a Million Quid

questions.explanation: The K Foundation, formed by Bill Drummond and Jimmy Cauty (formerly of The KLF), burned one million pounds in a disused boathouse on the Isle of Jura in Scotland on 23 August 1994, as a controversial and much-debated act of conceptual art.

questions.explanation: The name 'Bovril' combines the Latin word 'bos/bovis' (ox/cattle) with 'Vril,' the fictional life-energy force from Edward Bulwer-Lytton's 1871 novel 'The Coming Race,' which also inspired later occult and conspiracy theories about secret societies and Nazi UFOs.

questions.prompt:
Which unusual article does the following describe?

This subject concerns a notorious 18th-century London haunting that became a public sensation in 1762. Strange knocking and scratching sounds reported in a house were attributed to the spirit of a woman who had died under suspicious circumstances, with the ghost allegedly accusing her common-law husband of poisoning her. The case attracted enormous public attention, drawing crowds, satirists, and prominent figures of the day, including the writer and lexicographer Samuel Johnson, who took part in an investigation to determine whether the events were genuine. The affair was eventually exposed as a hoax orchestrated by the family living in the house, leading to criminal prosecution.
questions.hint: The correct answer is not associated with the United States; both the Amityville Haunting and the Bell Witch are American cases, not this one.
questions.explanation: The Cock Lane ghost was a supposed haunting in London in 1762 involving strange knockings attributed to the spirit of Fanny Lynes, who was said to have been poisoned by William Kent. It became a huge public sensation, investigated by figures including Samuel Johnson, before being revealed as a hoax perpetrated by Richard Parsons and his family.
